2608.21106.title: Atom Learning Model (ALM): how a real classroom got tokenised
2608.21106.paper_summary: The Atom Learning Model (ALM) tokenises a school curriculum. Two secondary mathematics textbooks were read by machine into 1,934 atoms, each one thing a learner can do in a single step, ordered by 4,616 machine-written prerequisite links. Both sides of a lesson are then expressed in that one structure: a question is a set of atoms plus everything beneath them, a child's ability is a score between 0 and 1 on every atom of the same graph, and whether a question suits a child is arithmetic over one index, with no difficulty parameter fitted for either side. Nobody wrote an atom, a link or a question. Reading the 757 pages cost £55, building the whole structure cost between £615 and £1,230, and against it the system composed 6,648 questions for 373 children in two English secondary schools over seven weeks, at 26p per composed question. Four measurements went against expectation. The cost is in the links, not the pages. The composer's own difficulty label has a rank correlation of -0.0123 with measured facility, so a language model shown a question cannot say how hard it is. Children stop working when a mark takes seven seconds instead of three. And the deployment never served a question deeper than two prerequisite steps, which is exactly where the central premise becomes testable, leaving it unfalsified rather than confirmed.
2608.21106.paper_summary_zh: 原子學習模型（ALM）將學校課程進行標記化。兩本中學數學教科書被機器讀取並轉換為1,934個原子，每個原子代表學習者在單一步驟中可以做的一件事，並按照4,616個機器生成的前置鏈接進行排序。課程的雙方都以這一結構表達：問題是一組原子加上它們之下的所有內容，孩子的能力是在同一圖表上每個原子的0到1之間的分數，而問題是否適合孩子則是對一個指數的算術運算，兩邊都沒有適合的難度參數。沒有人編寫過原子、鏈接或問題。閱讀這757頁的內容花費了55英鎊，構建整個結構的成本在615到1,230英鎊之間，而系統在七週內為兩所英國中學的373名學生生成了6,648個問題，每個生成的問題成本為26便士。有四個測量結果與預期相悖。成本在於鏈接，而不是頁面。創作者自己的難度標籤與測量的能力之間的排名相關性為-0.0123，因此向語言模型展示一個問題無法判斷其難度。當一個標記的處理時間從三秒變為七秒時，孩子們會停止工作。而且，部署從未提供過深於兩個前置步驟的問題，這正是中心前提變得可測試的地方，從而使其未被證偽而不是被確認。
2608.21106.author: Philipp Bogdan et.al.
